mainEntity.name: Are there specific design considerations for a tiny home built for year-round primary residence?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, building a tiny home for year-round primary residence requires specific design considerations to ensure comfort, durability, and energy efficiency. This includes robust insulation for varying temperatures, a well-designed HVAC system for heating and cooling, and potentially larger fresh and grey water tanks if off-grid. High-quality, durable materials are essential to withstand continuous use. Furthermore, optimizing natural light, ventilation, and storage solutions are crucial for long-term liveability. Our design process focuses on creating efficient and comfortable spaces tailored for primary residency.
acceptedAnswer.description: Year-round primary residence tiny homes need robust insulation, efficient HVAC, durable materials, and optimized natural light, ventilation, and storage for comfort and energy efficiency.
